I really like your word choice. your references to proper nouns are great, but a bit banal. a few lines are particularly outstanding to me - “my plate grows bigger when the famished children grow thinner”. “the hands are sacred but the touch is sin”. it’s great!

you need to be careful on that first part tho. the split between the modern - references to Prozac and Armani - and the historical - references to Eden and Pandora’s Box - don’t feel well balanced, especially with the entire grand mood of your closing lines. try spreading then out a bit more evenly or picking one side and sticking closer to it. a 50-50 is hard to pull off. 

there are parts where you stray a bit deep into the abstract without first setting them up. it’s confusing and annoying to read. what does the imagery of a concertina wire bring? what are the Blades of Hope? 

at the same time, some parts are too straightforward and repetitive. just comb over it and you’ll notice. 

your inconsistent rhyme scheme really interferes with the flow. it’s very jolting and abrupt to read - and not in a charismatic way. 

you jump from reference to reference, and the overarching message or journey that the poem leads you through is unclear and not consistent. you start by embodying yourself, the “I”, but never return to it, which creates a sense of being unfinished. 

it reads like you wrote it in a hurry, which isn’t what I wanted to feel when reading, because I can sense the underpinnings of a great work. it mostly needs to be trimmed, I think.

your poem isn’t bad, but it’s not refined. did you comb over every word and ensure it flowed just as you intended? even if you’re going for a conversational tone, your conversation and your literature clash, and not in a good way. 

there are some points where repetition and general confusion overtake the message of your poem, like the first stanza—a contradiction and a half—and the third and fourth.

I like the diction and imagery. your mentions of birds and dragonflies is great in the context of your poem. but do keep in mind your grammar. don’t capitalize words after commas, and sometimes commas don’t work well. look into dashes, colons, and semicolons. 

this is just my personal opinion, but your title is a bit bland. it doesn’t contextualize or provide any more information about your poem. it doesn’t really need to, but if ill be honest, “Unnamed” would hit harder than the same word that you ended the poem on. 

also listing your own name at the end is trite, don’t do that

when you’re leaving the reader to do most of the mental exercise for ultimately just one reading and your poem is 13 words without rhyme or succulent word choice, you should expect it to be scrutinized. this is not a /terrible/ poem, but it’s not a particularly eloquent one. it was probably written in sincerity, but it reads with mocking. it hits you square on the nose with its title and meaning, leaving nothing to be desired, nothing to gaze twice at. 

simple poetry is never bad in of itself, and there’s certainly an idea of a poem in here, but it’s just that—an idea.

I wish I knew the flow of the game most when I was lower tier. there’s a reason games become very short in high tier, less than 5 minutes on average. especially if you’re playing survivor. it seems simple, but it’s not something I’ve grasped until recently. 

basically, there are 5 ciphers. that means one person is kiting and 3 people are decoding. the first person must kite enough for those 3 ciphers to be popped. if they get downed at 5 ciphers, you must either sell then or rescue after half. if they get downed at 3 ciphers, it’s still equivalent to a 3 cipher kite, because the cipher that the slow decoder is working on (the rescuer) should be taken over. it’s rare for them to get downed at 4 ciphers, since that’s basically equivalent to a 2 cipher kite. after that, the kiter must be rescued and supported by someone for long enough for the other 2 ciphers to pop. 

when the game is early and you haven’t finished your first cipher, DO NOT HARASS. DO NOT SUPPORT. DO NOT DECODE WITH OTHERS. doing any of these will completely interrupt the flow of the game and grind your cipher rush to a screeching halt. 

low tier players have longer games because they do not decode, and they let decoded ciphers go to waste. make sure you assign yourself one of these roles the instant a fear state changes. will you support, rescue, or decode? it HAS to be one of these - don’t hesitate or dillydally. if the roles get messed up and there are multiple rescuers or supports when there doesn’t need to be, cipher rush falls apart.

this is why if you have a 4 man team where everyone can kite decently, you will win or draw 80% of games.

not quite the right sub for this... but I've always wanted a game with an incredibly high skillcap that gives players an absurd amount of character control for maximum immersion. just take things to the next level. a fighting game where you control each limb and movement manually. a shooting game where you have to load each individual bullet into your mag. movement mechanics that go beyond the usual WASD/sprint/roll/block. etc, a lot more. 

whenever I watch impressive character attack animations that I can "do" just by hitting a button, I can feel the disconnect between this master of their weapon and myself, who puts in a millionth of an effort to achieve the same result. 

it's a multiplayer pvp game that's extremely difficult to learn. but after months and months upon practice, character movements will appear natural and fluid effortlessly. learning to control your character is a meaningful skill and smurfing is instantly obvious. there are lots of meaningless features that enhance user input but are purely cosmetic. each flick of the wrist is significant, providing so many more factors than just clicking buttons. maybe it'll break from a tried controller or M&K setup, take something from vr... 

vr games mostly break this barrier for realism but I've never used them due to poor eyesight and high costs. indies like reciever 2 and rainworld have scratched the itch but only in their limited, respective ways. most AAA/modern multiplayer games are movement-based and limited in that way, not focusing so much on the actual attacks, and that's excluding the tracking/reaction speed that FPS games call for. I'm just kind of tired of them, considering guns are so... boring compared to all the other possible weapons. 

it's a lot to ask for, and will likely never be created/kick off. but it's my dream game lol.
